meta.boardFormat: Each board is a Claude Design 'dc' document. It has <script src=./support.js>, <link rel=stylesheet href=./xr-*.css> tags in <head>, a <helmet> that loads Google Fonts Public Sans 400/500/600/700, a 1-line <style> (body{margin:0} a{color:#1F4FD8}a:hover{color:#141B5E}) and an <x-dc> template with {{ }} bindings, <sc-if> and <sc-for>. Behaviour and sample data live in an inline <script type=text/x-dc data-dc-script> class that extends DCLogic.

boardConventions.stylesheetLinking: Each board links a cumulative subset in a fixed order. Counts by combination: foundation only = 15 boards (Batch 0 and others); +public = 15 (Batch 1); +workspace = 16 (Batch 2); +learning = 15 (Batch 3); +assess = 17 (Batch 4); +vendor = 11 (Batch 5); +govern = 16 (Batch 6); all 8 = 23 (Batch 7, Batch 8, Main). B8-07 load order: foundation, public, workspace, learning, assess, vendor, govern, admin. No board uses a class whose stylesheet it does not link (scan of all 128 boards).
globalOverridesWhenAllEightLoad: .xr-dpanel .xr-status wrap (xr-govern.css and xr-admin.css). In a product that loads all 8 sheets, this rule also applies to the B1-11, B3-11 and B4 decision panels, whose boards did not load it. Small deviation: long statuses wrap there too.
boardConventions.classNaming: BEM-like prefixed blocks. Each family has a prefix: xr- foundation, xp- public, xw- workspace, xl- learning, xa- assess, xv- vendor, xg- govern, xd- admin, plus canvas-only doc- and b1-. Elements use block-element names (xr-row-title, xr-dialog-foot). Modifiers use a double hyphen (xr-btn--primary, xr-status--ok, xr-fmt--compact, xr-side--rail, xr-tabs--on-white). There are 18 state classes: is-busy is-changed is-checked is-current is-diff is-done is-drawer is-err is-error is-focus is-latest is-no is-off is-ok is-primary is-selected is-shown is-zero. Shell states is-expanded and is-rail are set dynamically. Much styling hangs off ARIA attributes and states: aria-current, aria-selected, aria-pressed, aria-invalid, aria-disabled, [disabled], :has(input:checked), :has(input:focus-visible).
boardConventions.inlineStyles: 23,140 style= attributes across the boards, 1,128 distinct values. Frame chrome accounts for some: 'min-height: 900px' on .xr-app and .xr-shell (1,037), 'width: Npx; max-width: 100%' frame wrappers, and 'overflow-y: auto; height: Npx' crops. Most of the rest is product composition: margin:0 (4,127), display:flex (2,197), flex-direction:column (1,484), color:#40476B (1,382), gap:12px (835), grid-template-columns, max-width, padding, and status-tint overrides such as 'background:#E8F4EC;color:#1D6B45'. The 8 stylesheets alone do not reproduce the boards. The build needs an equivalent for this inline layout glue.
boardConventions.fonts: Every board loads https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Public+Sans:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap in <helmet>. Weights used in CSS: 400, 500, 600, 700. No italic is used (.xp-hero-h em sets font-style:normal).

notes: design/handoff-v46/canvas-v46/project/handoff/tokens.css, handoff/tokens.json and the xr-foundation.css :root block are identical: 65 = 65 = 65, same names and values (python comparison).

Only 11 of the 65 tokens are read through var() in any stylesheet: font-sans, font-mono, focus, focus-dark, e1, e2, e3, dur-1, dur-2, dur-3, ease. The other 54 are declared but not referenced. Colours, spacing, radii and layout sizes are literal values in the CSS and in board inline styles. Changing a colour token therefore changes nothing. Only the font token is a real swap point, as board 02 says: 'Replace it by changing --xr-font-sans only'.

Several values map to more than one token: #F4F5FB = canvas = surface-2; #1F4FD8 = link = focus = info; #8A5A05 = gold-700 = warn; #FBF3E0 = gold-50 = warn-bg; #F7C95B = gold-400 = focus-dark. Rewriting literals to var() therefore needs a human choice per use. It is not a mechanical translation.

Colours outside the token set appear in the stylesheets (see each sheet's nonTokenColours). Examples: #FAFBFE, #E8D3A3, #8F1C13 and #8F1B12, #EEF0FA, #E6E8F3, #FFFBF0, #FFF7F6, and in xr-public.css #D7DBF5, #AEB6EC, #EEF0FB, the tricolour #F2A33A/#7CC0E8/#E5323B and the atmospheres #173A6E/#233069.

Type scale (B8-07 and board 02): display 44/52/700 (public hero); h1 32/40/700; h2 22/30/700; h3 18/26/600; lead 18/28; body 16/24; label 15/20/600; small 14/20; meta 14/20 in ink-3; overline 13/16/700 uppercase; chip 13 bold (compact 12); caption 13/18. Phone scale below 600 px of app width: h1 26/34, h2 20/28, display 32/40. Public scale: xp-h1 48, xp-h2 44 (--sm 32), xp-h3 22, hero 54-62 (INFERRED from container overrides: 54 below 1280, 50 below 1024, 38 below 600).
Rule (board 02): real content never below 14 px, nothing functional below 12 px. Tabular figures for aligned numbers (.xr-num, .xl-num). Monospace only for record IDs (.xr-id).
No dark theme is designed. The product is light-first. .xr-dark marks navy bands only (record-hub header, inactive banner): 'Never a whole dark workspace' (board 01).

The repo placeholder token --xr-font-sans (commit 1b090c9) has the same name but a different value. The four other placeholder names (--xr-color-fg, --xr-color-bg, --xr-color-muted, --xr-space-unit) do not exist in v46.

components.name: Button
variants: tertiary text (underlined link style; instant, no busy state)
destructive red (only where authorised; always confirms)
destructive quiet (entry point to a confirm)
states: busy: spinner and verb label ('Giving access…') with aria-disabled
components.a11y: min-height 44 (sm 36), above the 24x24 target. Labels are verb plus object. Unavailable actions are hidden, or shown with the reason next to them, never as a silent grey button (board 03). Busy buttons ignore repeat presses (board 10). Button order: primary last (right) on wide screens; stacked full width with primary first on phones (board 03).

components.name: Icon button
components.a11y: Always has an accessible name such as 'Open menu', 'Close menu', 'Collapse menu' or 'Remove filter Status: …' (board 12).

components.name: Link, back link, jump link
variants: 'Go to decision' jump (shown below 860 content; moves focus to the panel)
external link with '(opens in a new tab)' for screen readers
components.a11y: Links are underlined in text. The back link names the destination, not 'Back' (board 03). External links say so (board 02).

components.name: Field (label, hint, error, optional)
variants: read-only value block ('Read-only · set at import')
states: invalid (aria-invalid=true plus a message under the field)
components.a11y: Labels above fields and always visible; no placeholder-only labels (09b AR-8). The error is in the field description (aria-describedby; 1,175 uses on the boards) and is announced.

components.name: Text input (text, email, search, date)
states: long value ends with an ellipsis
components.a11y: min-height 44, 16px text.

components.name: Select
components.a11y: Native <select> (appearance:none). Use a radio list when a short set of choices has long names (board 03).

components.name: Textarea
components.a11y: min-height 128, resize vertical.

components.name: File input
components.a11y: Native file input with a label and hint.

components.name: Checkbox and radio rows, choice cards, pick lists
variants: choice card (radio or check) with title and sub
components.a11y: The whole label is the target (44px). Radios move with arrow keys (board 12).

components.name: Labelled 1-5 scale
components.a11y: A real radio group in a fieldset with the statement as legend; every point has a number and a word; arrow keys. Words for points 2-4 are a proposal (board 13 Q6).

components.name: List toolbar (search, filters, More filters, filter chips, count)
variants: search plus up to 2 filters plus More filters
phone: search on its own row, then 1 filter and More filters; the 2nd filter moves into More filters
public catalogue filter sidebar, which becomes a sheet below 1024 xp
states: More filters open (aria-expanded, count in the button label 'More filters (1)')
components.a11y: Result count is in a role=status span ('5 of 214 students'). Chip remove buttons are 28x28 with aria-label 'Remove <label>'.

components.name: Segmented control
components.a11y: Never navigation (board 03).

components.name: Tabs
variants: section tabs: nav of links with aria-current=page that change the address
record tabs: board 03 specifies role=tablist with aria-selected and arrow keys
states: overflow: sideways scroll with right fade, left shade once scrolled, thin track, current tab scrolled into view
components.a11y: Section tabs are ordinary links (Tab between them). Record tabs use arrow keys (board 12). DIFFERENCE: the experiment-hub record tabs on B2-12 and B3-01 are drawn as <nav class='xr-tabs xw-hubtabs'> links, and no board draws role=tabpanel (29 tablists on 11 boards).

components.name: Stepper (guided flow)
states: phone: only the current label plus 'Step n of N'
components.a11y: aria-current on the current step.

components.name: DataTable with labelled rows
variants: editable table (unsaved / saved / not saved states; 'n unsaved changes · n needs fixing')
sortable column (B1-10 'Received' only: th aria-sort with a button)
states: loading (skeleton rows; aria-busy=true on the wrap)
labelled-row mode below 760 content (xp-compare: below 600 xp)
components.a11y: Visually hidden caption. Every row opens its record. B8-07: 'Below 760 px of content each row becomes a labelled block'. The B1-10 defect lives here (see b1_10). Sort is stated in the header row (09a AR-2).

components.name: Rows / attention list
states: all clear ('Nothing needs you right now')
components.a11y: Rows always open something. AR-1 budget: 5-6 rows or fewer, one action each.

components.name: Status chip
states: long text wraps inside a decision panel (govern/admin rule)
components.a11y: Always a word. Icon shape and lightness differ by tone, never colour alone (board 04). Words follow the B8-03 vocabulary.

components.name: Format chip (WEB, AR, VR, MR)
variants: normal: offered by the experiment (indigo tint)
states: static; the chip does not change on completion (the status word beside it does)
components.a11y: Code plus glyph plus words. 'Available in' is not entitlement (board 04, B8-03).

components.name: Notice
variants: refused-with-reason (quoted reason, who, when, next action)
components.a11y: role=status for success and info (1,883 on the boards); role=alert for errors (396). Success uses a notice in place, never a toast that vanishes (board 04).

components.name: Error summary
components.a11y: role=alert with tabindex=-1 so focus can move to it. The rule (boards 12 and B8-07) is that summary links move focus to the field. DIFFERENCE: of 192 xw-errsum instances, 115 link to fields and 77 do not (47 without links or tabindex, for example B5-03; 30 without links but with tabindex, for example B2-05).

components.name: Shell banner (paused, inactive)
variants: paused (amber): 'Your institution’s access is paused — your work is kept.' + Help
inactive (navy): 'Your account is inactive. Contact your institution administrator.' + Help
components.a11y: role=status. It is a GL-01 shell banner, never a modal (B8-07).

components.name: Empty, loading, failed, no-match states
variants: empty: icon, one line, one next step
loading: skeleton shaped like the content, announced politely
failed: notice in place, 'Try again' and 'Report a problem'
components.a11y: Loading is announced ('Loading your reports'). No error codes or '500' (board 04).

components.name: Message page (AR-10)
states: inside the shell (nothing current in the sidebar) or under the public header
components.a11y: One H1, one sentence, one primary action named by its destination, optional Help link. The icon is decorative.

components.name: Dialog DL-1 / DL-2 / DL-3
variants: DL-1 confirm (one sentence on the effect)
DL-1 destructive (red button; initial focus on Cancel)
DL-2 confirm with a required reason (says who will see it)
DL-3 small edit (two fields at most; Enter in the field saves)
states: validation error (focus to the first invalid field)
closed (focus back to the trigger, success notice on the page)
phone: bottom sheet at full width, buttons stacked with the confirming action on top, at most one field below 600
components.a11y: Board 10 uses <dialog> with showModal(), aria-labelledby and aria-describedby. Product boards draw a div with role=dialog and aria-modal=true inside a frame scrim. Cancel is first and quiet (xr-btn--text); the confirming action is last. Never used for navigation, scrolling forms or long lists (board 10, B8-07).

components.name: Inline panel
variants: mid-page confirmation or reason beside the affected row
components.a11y: B8-07: 'Mid-page confirmations and reasons, beside the row they affect'.

components.name: Decision page and panel (AR-4)

b1_10.rootCause: Labelled-row mode hides the table header visually but leaves it in the tab order. Below 760 px of content width (the xr-content container), xr-foundation.css applies '.xr-table thead{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0 0 0 0)}' and switches table, tbody, tr and td to display:block. Clipping is a visually-hidden technique that keeps elements in the accessibility tree and in the tab order. On B1-10 the 'Received' column header holds a real <button> (sort toggle). That button stays focusable while it is clipped to a 1x1 invisible box, so a keyboard user can focus an invisible control. No rule removes it from the tab order and no visible equivalent is rendered at that width.

options.name: Port the 8 xr-*.css files verbatim as global, layered CSS in packages/ui. React components emit the same class names.
options.fidelity: Highest. The rules are the frozen bytes, and the class and DOM contract matches the boards one to one, so board markup is a direct spec for components.
options.visualRegressionParity: Best. Boards and product run the same CSS. Remaining pixel differences come from the composition layer (inline styles) and data.
options.maintainability: Good if guarded. Prefix families (xr-, xp-, xw-, xl-, xa-, xv-, xg-, xd-) avoid collisions. A checksum test against design/handoff-v46/MANIFEST.json prevents drift. Deviations live in one additive 'product' layer. The canvas-only rules (doc-*, b1-*, is-focus, board controls) ship as dead weight (about 10 KB); a lint rule bans those classes in product code.
options.cost: Low. The CSS is ready-made; the work is components and composition.
options.risks: Global namespace, hard-coded hex values, and canvas positioning rules (drawer, scrim, dialog scrim) that need product overrides.

options.name: CSS Modules (rewrite each component's rules into co-located .module.css)
options.fidelity: Medium. A manual rewrite of about 1,330 rules, with many cross-component and context selectors (.xr-top .xr-acct-btn, .xr-shell.is-drawer > .xr-side, .xw-hubhead .xr-h1, .xr-dpanel .xr-status, .xp-dark :focus-visible, .xr-toolbar > .xr-field) that need :global or restructuring. Container names must stay global anyway.
options.visualRegressionParity: Lower. Every rewritten rule can drift, and class names no longer match the boards, so reviewers cannot diff markup.
options.maintainability: Good locality, but two sources of truth (boards and modules).
options.risks: Silent regressions in container-query interplay and cascade order across the 8 sheets.

options.name: Translate to Tailwind 4 theme and utilities
options.fidelity: Low to medium. 65 tokens map to @theme easily, but most CSS uses literal hex values that map to several tokens. Container queries need named-container variants (@max-[760px]/xr-content:). :has(), sibling/descendant contexts, ::file-selector-button, scrollbar styling, sticky fades and attribute-state selectors become very long class strings or arbitrary variants.
options.visualRegressionParity: Weak. The translation has to be proven pixel by pixel.
options.maintainability: Poor for this design: huge class lists, no 1:1 trace to board markup, and an ambiguous token choice for every hex value.
options.risks: High. It also conflicts with Tailwind Preflight unless Preflight is disabled.

cssStrategy.recommendation: Option 1. Copy the 8 stylesheets byte for byte into packages/ui (for example packages/ui/src/styles/v46/) with the art/ folder next to them so the relative url("art/…") paths resolve. Import them in B8-07 load order through one entry stylesheet that assigns cascade layers: @layer xr.foundation, xr.public, xr.workspace, xr.learning, xr.assess, xr.vendor, xr.govern, xr.admin, xr.product, utilities; then @import url(xr-foundation.css) layer(xr.foundation); and so on. xr.product is a small additive stylesheet owned by the build. It holds only documented production deltas: the B1-10 DataTable sort fix, .xr-app min-height 100dvh, fixed-position drawer and scrim, bottom-sheet dialog below 600 app width plus the dialog alignment variants, drawer/dialog/menu motion under the reduced-motion guard, a gold focus ring inside .xr-side, the .xp overflow fix if verification confirms the sticky issue, the @font-face for Public Sans, and the decision on the sticky versus static decision panel. Each delta cites its board or finding. Add a Vitest test that hashes the 8 copied files against design/handoff-v46/MANIFEST.json and fails on any edit. React components in packages/ui emit exactly the board class names and ARIA attributes. Component props map to modifiers (variant='primary' to xr-btn--primary) and state to is-* or ARIA attributes.
rationale: Fidelity is guaranteed by construction. The board is the authority, and the same CSS with the same markup gives the same render.
Visual-regression parity: the remaining diffs isolate real product differences.
Reviewability: board markup can be compared line by line with component output.
B8-06 says 'build ... without re-inventing the visual system'. Board 13 change #27 made one shared stylesheet the system.

The cascade layers keep the internal order of the 8 sheets and let composition utilities override component defaults, the way board inline styles do. !important inside the xr layers still wins, which matches inline-style versus !important behaviour.
cssStrategy.tailwindDisposition: Keep Tailwind 4 (already installed: tailwindcss 4.3.3, @tailwindcss/postcss 4.3.3) only as a composition-utility layer that replaces board inline styles, and remove Preflight. Replace "@import 'tailwindcss'" in apps/web/src/app/globals.css with explicit layered imports of theme and utilities only: '@import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme); @import "tailwindcss/utilities.css" layer(utilities);'. Preflight would remove list markers that boards rely on (inline-styled <ul style='padding-left:20px'> in error notices, .xv-los), set svg and img to display:block, and reset headings and buttons, which changes board rendering. Constrain @theme to v46: clear the default palette (--color-*: initial) and expose only the 38 xr colours; keep the 4px spacing base (Tailwind's 0.25rem equals the xr 4px scale); fonts from --xr-font-sans and --xr-font-mono; radii 4/6/8/12; shadows e1-e3. Allowed use: app-level layout glue that mirrors board inline styles (flex, grid, gap, margin, max-width, width). Not allowed: colour, typography or component styling in packages/ui components, which use xr classes only. Enforce with a lint rule or a grep test. If the owner prefers fewer moving parts, the alternative is to remove Tailwind and copy board inline style objects verbatim into React style props, plus 3 layout primitives (Stack, Cluster, Grid). That gives the highest fidelity but is worse to maintain, and CSP needs style-src-attr. Either way this updates open decision E-19 ('Tailwind v4 + tokens in @xr/ui; primitives chosen at Design V2 start') and should be recorded in an ADR.
packaging: packages/ui/package.json exports './styles.css' (the layered entry), './styles/v46/*' and the art/ and fonts/ folders, and lists them in 'files'. Today only './tokens.css' to './src/tokens.css' is exported.
Replace the placeholder tokens.css: the v46 :root comes from xr-foundation.css itself. Keep no second token file, or keep handoff/tokens.css as a documentation copy only.

Self-host Public Sans (OFL) woff2 for 400/500/600/700 via @font-face with family name exactly 'Public Sans', so --xr-font-sans stays verbatim. next/font would rename the family and change the token value. Preload the latin file(s).
